tossups.text: Hilbert's Grand Hotel paradox is a thought experiment concerning this concept in sets, and taking the limit to it is used to find a function's horizontal asymptote. Irrational numbers are defined to have this quantity of digits, and Euclid proved that there are this many prime numbers. For 10 points, name this concept in math which is defined as the largest, boundless quantity.

this structure is essential for hypodermis function. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this epidermis-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The epidermis is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in hypodermis function.

tossups.text: One character in this play declares "I shudder when I think that the earth takes a whole day to rotate. What a waste of time!" A doctor in this play chastises the title character for "pissing in the street" and enrols him on a scientific experiment where he can only eat peas. Two characters in this play are spotted dancing at the Horse and Stars tavern. Karl Emil Franzos added the stage direction "He drowns" to the end of this play, after the title character swims out into a lake to hide a knife used to kill his lover Marie, who has been cheating with the Drum Major. For 10 points, name this unfinished play about a murderous military barber, written by Georg Büchner and adapted into an opera by Alban Berg.

In a short story by this author, the narrator realizes that he is "driven and derided by vanity" in his quest to buy a gift for Mangan's sister. He wrote Father Arnall's fire-and-brimstone sermon into his novel that begins with a nursery story about Baby Tuckoo. This author created a character who climaxes during a bottle rocket explosion in a novel in which Blazes Boylan has an affair with the protagonist's wife, Molly. For 10 points, name this author of "Araby," who created Stephen Dedalus and Leopold Bloom in his novels A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man and Ulysses.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for anterior pituitary hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hypothalamus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hypothalamus is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in anterior pituitary hormones.

tossups.text: In one poem by this author, the titular group "makes no sound but the panting like a silken serpent" and Carola, a prostitute, blackmails Dantés in one of his plays. A more famous work features a barber shop-educated boy who starts a nonviolent revolution, Octavio Sansur. In addition to "The Indians come down from Mixco",Chantaje, and The Eyes of the Interred, a 1949 novel sees Nicho Aquino find Gaspar Ilón, who earlier helped the Indians grow their corn. Besides a series about a United Fruit Company-dominated Latin America, one of the first scenes of his best known story features several beggars on the steps of a church. The titular character of that work, who only appears six times in the novel, uses death of military officer to get to Carvajal, who he also intends to kill. For 10 points, name this author of "The Banana Trilogy", Men of Maize, and El Señor Presidente, a Guatemalan Nobel laureate.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for nail anatomy. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hair follicle-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hair follicle is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in nail anatomy.

tossups.text: This man's roommate, who fought in the Second Anglo-Afghan War, is disdainful of his strong addictions to opiates. This man met Irene Adler, the only woman to beat him in a battle of wits, in the story "A Scandal in Bohemia". This man dies in combat with his rival Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls. For 10 points, name this detective created by Arthur Conan Doyle and accompanied by John Watson.

This man was seriously injured as a youth under Francisco de Almeida on India's Malabar Coast, and again at the Battle of Diu, which required a four-month recovery in Cochin. This man was championed by Bishop Juan Rodriguez de Fonseca, who nonetheless retained nationalist suspicion towards him. This figure converted Rajah Humabon to Christianity and along with Rui Faleiro secured funding for his major effort from Emperor Charles V. That expedition was abandoned by the San Antonio before the Trinidad, Concepcion and Victoria reached the Peru Current. This man died in battle against Lapu-Lapu, but his expedition was completed by Juan Sebastian del Cano. For 10 points, name this leader of the first voyage to circumnavigate the Earth.

In an East Nigerian folk tale, a bush rat named Oyot boils himself alive after Emiong, who is one of these creatures, lies to him about how he makes his soup so delicious. In Book 4 of Ovid's Metamorphoses, Bacchus turns the daughters of Minyas into these animals when they refuse to participate in a festival dedicated to him. In the Popol Vuh, a messenger that resembles this animal negotiates a deal in which mankind offers their armpits and waists in exchange for fire. The Mayan god of death, Camazotz, takes the form of this animal and lends his name to a creature that decapitates Hunahpu when he travels to Xibalba with his twin brother. For ten points, name these flying mammals that are often associated with vampires.

Charles Lamb misquotes this poem in his essay "The Old Benchers of the Inner Temple," as its fifth stanza actually begins "what wond'rous life in this I lead!" The volta of this poem is the sixth stanza, which sublimates the idea of a symmetrical submarine creation with an internal rhyme in the line "the mind, an ocean where each kind / does straight its own resemblance find / yet it creates, transcending these, / far other worlds, and other seas." The first stanza of this poem delineates the prizes of the martyr, conqueror, and poet - "the palm, the oak, or bays" - but notes that they are inferior to "the garlands of repose." Its third stanza notes that to carve a mistress's name into a tree is to deface the native beauty of the tree itself. This poem's final lines are "how could such sweet and wholesome hours / be reckoned but with herbs and flowers!" For 10 points, name this poem by Andrew Marvell that imagines man as happiest alone in Eden.

Frederick Charles of Hessen was invited to become the monarch of this country during World War I, but that offer was rescinded after Germany was defeated. The 1809 Peace of Hamina led to this country becoming a semi-autonomous Grand Duchy of Russia. This country's independence was facilitated by a military victory at Tampere [TAHM-pe-re] by Karl Mannerheim, namesake of a defensive fortification used by this country in its Winter War against the Soviets. For 10 points, what easternmost Scandinavian country is governed from Helsinki?

The approximate magnitude of this effect is given by a factor equal to the expectation value of the exponential of minus the square of the direct product of the scattering vector and initial scattering center displacement. That factor gives the fraction of scattered particles experiencing this effect and is named for Waller and Debye. Zeeman splitting due to nuclear magnetic fields can be measured by this effect combined with the Doppler effect, a measurement known as its namesake spectroscopy. This effect is a momentum-space analogue of zero-phonon optical emission. It was first observed in solid iridium, which was found to exhibit sharp resonances like gases in x-rays. For 10 points, name this phenomenon in which a certain fraction of gamma rays emitted by atoms in a solid are emitted recoil-free, an effect named for its German discoverer who won the 1961 Nobel Prize in Physics.

By using data from NASA's Advanced Composition Explorer, Ko and collaborators were able to differentiate two forms of this phenomenon by using estimated velocity fluctuations. The strength of this phenomenon is correlated with the luminosity of the accretion disk for T Tauri stars. One form of this phenomenon varies in its density, temperature and ionization state and originates in certain, funnel-like "holes." Due to intense radiation pressure, Wolf-Rayet stars exhibit a powerful version of this phenomenon, which causes them to lose mass at a high rate. The magnetic reconnection in Earth's magnetotail caused by this phenomenon can cause aurorae. For 10 points, name this phenomenon in which a flow of charged particles are ejected from the corona of a star.

Farmers were given the right to engage in these events by the Frazier-Lemke Act of 1934. Following these events, FpML guidelines mandate that SubTier1 stakeholders are lowest in seniority and thus have the lowest priority. A 2005 paper co-authored by Elizabeth Warren argued that individuals who start these events were likely to have had a medical emergency. The US code governing these events allows for an automatic stay. On September 15, 2008, the largest one of these proceedings in US history was started by Lehman Brothers. These events may be followed by a reorganization in the Chapter 11 type, unlike Chapter 7, which leads to liquidation. For 10 points, name this legal process in which debtors obtain relief from their creditors.
acceptableAnswers: answers like engaging in bankruptcy proceedings
prompt on answers like going into debt

tossups.text: The "dropping" form of this device contains a tube connecting the bottom to the top, equalizing pressure. Partitioning immiscible [ih-MISS-uh-bul] liquids can be done using the separatory types of this device. Another form of this device contains a flat porous surface connecting the input to the output, is used in conjunction with a vacuum pump, is named for Ernst Büchner [BYOOK-nur], and is outfitted with filter paper. A rubber adapter often enhances the seal between this device and a flask. For 10 points, name this cone-shaped piece of lab equipment that guides a liquid through a narrow opening.

This man's mummified face ended up in Nicholas Armez's possession. This non-monarch was the target of a botched plot by his one-time sidekick, the Marquis of Cinq-Mars. He set up the "Company of One Hundred Associates" and negotiated the Peace of Alais, which limited civil rights. This man's career barely survived the "Day of the Dupes" in which he had a tense meeting with Marie de' Medici. In support of explorers like Samuel de Champlain, this man founded the Company of New France. He personally commanded French troops as they besieged the Huguenot stronghold at La Rochelle. This man, the "Red Eminence," was succeeded by his protégé, Jules Mazarin. For 10 points, name this French clergyman who was Louis XIII's chief minister.

One character by this playwright regrets modeling for the sculpture "Resurrection Day" and is killed by an avalanche along with the sculptor Arnold. Calls to smash a character's windows end one act of a play by this author that sees Petra's father ostracized for reporting the tannery's contamination of the public baths. A character by this author commits suicide at Madame Diana's brothel after the wife of George Tesman burns his manuscript. That title character later shoots herself with Judge Brack's pistols. For 10 points, name this Norwegian playwright of When We Dead Awaken, A Public Enemy, and Hedda Gabler.

This city is bordered to the east by Biscayne Bay, which separates this city from another city known as its "Beach". This city is the seat of Dade County and its seal and flag feature a palm tree. This city, which has been nicknamed the "Capital of Latin America," has a large population of Cuban-Americans. For 10 points, name this most populous metropolis in Florida, a seaport on Florida's southeastern tip.

In one work by this artist, a king lounges on his bed as his guards slay his horses and some naked ladies. In addition to The Death of Sardanapalus, this artist depicted burning towns in the background of a work showing an ottoman on horseback slaying scantily clad Greeks, Massacre at Chios. For 10 points, name this artist who may be most famous for a painting containing a young boy with two pistols following a woman carrying the French flag, Liberty Leading the People.

parts.text: You'll need one of these compounds to let you know when the titration has reached the equivalence point.Turmeric can be used as one of these, but you'll more likely use litmus paper.
The indicator will allow you to notice when this value changes within a certain range. This value is 7 for apurely neutral chemical, and is lower than 7 for an acid.
When working with a very basic solution, this indicator will be your friend. This chemical turns a clearsolution bright pink at a pH between ten and twelve, and colorless otherwise.

bonuses.leadin: Congratulations: your chemistry teacher trusts you with dispensing chemicals, and now it's time to do anacid-base titration, for ten points each!

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with cerebral cortex lobes.
What is the main function of the cerebrum in the nervous system?
Name another component of the nervous system related to cerebral cortex lobes.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human nervous system.

parts.text: Also known as the Sons of Ben, what group of poets earned their appellation due to their support of Charles I during the English Civil War?
While imprisoned in 1642 for supporting the Royalists, which Cavalier poet wrote "To Althea, from Prison." He also wrote "To Lucasta, on Going to the Wars."
Among this Cavalier poet's claims to fame are inventing the game of cribbage and writing the "Ballad upon a Wedding."

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following questions about 17th century British poetry, For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this set of six somber works that includes "I Wake and Feel the Fell of Dark, Not Day" and "Carrion Comfort" and were written during their author's time as a professor at University College Dublin.
The Terrible Sonnets were written by this poet of "The Wreck of the Deutschland," who frequently used sprung rhythm in poems like "The Windhover."

This poem by Hopkins states that "the world is charged" with the title entity, which "will flame out" and "gather to a greatness, like the ooze of oil." It describes the Holy Ghost brooding with "warm breast" and "bright wings."

bonuses.leadin: A poem in this group compares the narrator's laments to "dead letters sent / To dearest him that lives alas! away." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with adrenal medulla hormones.
What is the main function of the adrenal in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to adrenal medulla hormones.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name this novel about a womanizer from the Caucasus Mountains whose love interests include Princess Mary and Bela. Grushnitsky ("groosh-NIT-skee") falls off a cliff at the end of his duel with this novel's title character .

Pechorin is the title superfluous man of Mikhail Lermontov's A Hero of Our Time, which drew inspiration from this other poet's Eugene Onegin ("oh-NAY-ghin"). Lermontov wrote the poem The Death of the Poet after this author died in a duel.

Isaiah Berlin considered superfluous-men foils like Tolstoy's Levin and Pushkin's Lensky to be prototyped on this literary critic in his essay The Remarkable Decade. Dostoyevsky ("doh-stuh-YEV-skee") was sent to Siberia for reading a letter written by this critic during a meeting of the Petrashevsky ("pet-ruh-SHEV-skee") Circle.

bonuses.leadin: This novel's main character was named after a river in Northern Russia as homage to another author's Eugene Onegin ("oh-NAY-ghin") being named after the river Onega. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with allergies and hypersensitivity.
What is the main function of the vaccine in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to allergies and hypersensitivity.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name this author of The Satanic Verses.

This other Rushdie novel features Shiva-of-the-Knees, Parvati-the-witch, and the telepathic Saleem Sinai, all of whom have special powers because they were born at the title hour of India's independence and partition.
In Midnight's Children, Saleem has this gigantic facial feature, which is constantly dripping and extremely sensitive.

bonuses.leadin: One of this author's novels opens with Jibreel Farishta and Saladin Chamcha falling from a plane crash, and that work resulted in a fatwa being placed on this author's head. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this retrovirus-caused disease that claimed hundreds of thousands of lives in the 1980s and 1990s during its namesake "crisis."

In 1985, Ryan White was prevented from entering his middle school in this state because he had contracted AIDS. In the 1920's this state became a base for the KKK under the leadership of D.C. Stephenson.
Mary Fisher advocated for compassion towards HIV positive people and greater awareness of AIDS at two of these events. Pat Buchanan gave his "culture war" speech at the 1992 edition of this event.

bonuses.leadin: This disease killed Rock Hudson, who left 250,000 dollars to help found an organization that tries to combat its main cause. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Though he'd be defeated by the Wax Girl, this African spider god was pretty tricky, and perhaps created the first human with the help of his dad Nyame.
This son of Iapetus and Themis stole fire from the gods to give to humans and, afterwards, had his liver repeatedly eaten.
This Welsh god of agriculture, the son of Don, stole a hound, a deer, and a bird from Arawn and thus kicked off the Battle of the Trees, in which his brother Gwydion turned the trees into fighters.

bonuses.leadin: Name some assorted figures from myth who caused trouble, For 10 points each.

parts.text: Reuben Borne feels guilty about not honoring his promise to the deceased title character in this short story.
The scientist Aylmer begins to despise the titular imperfection in this story that ends with the death of his wife.
Both "Roger Malvin's Burial" and "The Birthmark" are stories from Mosses from an Old Manse, a collection by what author of The Scarlet Letter?

bonuses.leadin: Both main characters in this story are returning from Lovell's Fight, though the title character dies along the way. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man who was succeeded as UK Prime Minister by James Callaghan.

Harold Wilson sent British troops to this constituent nation of the United Kingdom in 1969 as part of Operation Banner. Operation Banner was intended to support the Royal Ulster Constabulary in this constituent nation of the UK.
Harold Wilson succeeded this leader of the Labour Party after he died suddenly in 1963. This politician held the position of Minister of Fuel and Power during the "bitter winter" of 1946-1947.

bonuses.leadin: This man was made Baron of Rievaulx upon his resignation as Prime Minister. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this technique, formalized by Kenneth Wilson, which is used to eliminate infnities in physical theories.
The most famous use of renormalization is probably Feynman, Tomonaga, and Schwinger's work on the quantum theory of this fundamental feld, whose force is mediated by the photon.
Renormalization theory can be used to show that this quantity becomes infnite at the critical point; this quantity can be viewed as the scale on which order exists in a physical system.

bonuses.leadin: The basic idea behind this technique is to pick a scale cutof and derive a relationship between the coupling constants and the cutof so that the coupling constants in front of problematic terms goes to zero as the cutof increases. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this quantity that is about 300 millions meters per second. This quantity squared times mass equals the energy of a stationary object.

This word describes a velocity that is allowed to exceed the speed of light since it does not transmit information. Plane waves are given by the equation A times the exponential of k dot r minus omega t plus phi, where phi accounts for a "shift" described by this word.
Two

parts.text: Name this experiment by John Watson and Rosalie Rayner, in which the threat of a loud gong conditioned a baby to cry loudly at the sight of rats.
Little Albert was evidence for this school of psychology inspired by Ivan Pavlov's dogs, which regarded the analysis of cognition as unscientific.

Another experiment involving dog behavior, run by Martin Seligman, tested this phenomenon, in which dogs accustomed to electric shock and restraint would not escape the shocks even after the restraints were gone.

bonuses.leadin: Eventually, the baby in question displayed generalized fear of furry objects like Santa Claus beards. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this planet that contains the Caloris Basin, which will eventually be orbited by the MESSENGER spacecraft.
This planet was reclassified into a dwarf planet in 2006, and is orbited by the moon Charon. Its eccentric orbit can bring it closer to the Sun than Neptune.
Pluto is also orbitting by these two smaller moons, discovered by the Hubble Space Telescope's Pluto Companion Search Team. Name both.

bonuses.leadin: Most of what we know about this planet was obtained by the first spacecraft to visit it, the Mariner 10. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this conflict between a chief of the Sauk people and the United States over disputed territory ceded in the Treaty of St. Louis.

As a Colonel in the Black Hawk War, this man was under the command of General Henry Atkinson and resisted Jefferson Davis' attempts to woo his daughter during that period. This victor at the battle of Palo Alto later died after drinking an excessive amount of iced milk and mixed fruits at an 1850 presidential fundraiser.
This other man saw his only service in a war as a militia captain during the Black Hawk War. This attorney later defeated men like Stephen Douglas and John Bell in the Election of 1860.

bonuses.leadin: This conflict began when a delegation of Natives in the so-called "British Band" were attacked by a militia at Stillman's Run. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this genre of poem, a lament for someone who has died. Thomas Gray wrote one of these poems "in a country churchyard."

This elegy by John Milton was written for his friend Edward King. Most of this poem is spoken by an "uncouth swain" who comes to pluck berries "harsh and crude" and instructs the title figure to "Look homeward, Angel."

This poet wrote "tis better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all" in his elegy "In Memoriam A.H.H." He described the title king's desire "to strive, to seek, to find, and not to yield" in a more famous poem.

bonuses.leadin: Pearl, an early allegorical poem of this type in English, is thought to be dedicated to the poet's daughter, and describes how the title gem "slipped from me through grass to ground." For 10 points each:

parts.text: This east-coast state began producing peaches as early as the 1500s, earning it its nickname of "The Peach State."
This state's motto "Eureka!" is a reference to the gold found here. That discovery also gave this state its nickname of "The Golden State."
The Buffalo National River and the Boston Mountains helped give this state its nickname of "The Natural State."

bonuses.leadin: Some American states are known by state nicknames. For 10 points each, answer these questions about some of those nicknames.

parts.text: Name this 1959 Jazz album that featured Bill Evans on piano and John Coltrane and Cannonball Adderley on Saxophone.
Kind of Blue is an album by this legendary musician and bandleader whose other works include Sketches of Spain and Birth of the Cool.
Miles Davis played this instrument, also famously played by Louis Armstrong on such tracks as "What a Wonderful World."

bonuses.leadin: It featured tracks such as "Freddy Freeloader" and "Flamenco Sketches," for 10 points each:
